foreign_state_stake.note: In August 2013 Sekunjalo Independent Media bought 55 percent of Independent News & Media South Africa, the Public Investment Corporation 25 percent and two Chinese state owned companies, CADF and CITVC, 20 percent (Mail & Guardian). amaBhungane named Interacom Holdings, made up of CADF and CITVC, as the 20 percent shareholder in 2019 (https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2019-11-14-pic-wants-to-investigate-sekunjalo-directors-after-liquidation/), and in July 2026 Daily Maverick still described Interacom as a minority shareholder backed by Chinese investors; no source found reports a sale. Disputed for IOL itself: amaBhungane reported in 2018 that Independent transferred Independent Online to Sagarmatha Technologies, majority owned by Iqbal Survé's family trust, in which Independent held 4.1 percent after a share issue on 31 December 2016 (https://amabhungane.org/iqbal-surves-mythical-beast/); IOL says it has operated as an independent digital publisher, with its own ownership structure, since 2014 (Daily Maverick, 7 June 2026, https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-06-07-iols-r200m-expansion-plan-marks-another-turn-in-the-sekunjalo-media-saga/); Freedom House still described IOL as Independent Media's digital version in 2022 (https://freedomhouse.org/country/south-africa/beijings-global-media-influence/2022). No source found gives Independent's holding in Sagarmatha after 2016 or documents a Chinese state stake in the company that owns IOL now. The record is about ownership; it is not a finding that the shareholders direct what IOL publishes.

foreign_state_stake.note: In August 2013 Sekunjalo Independent Media bought 55 percent of Independent News & Media South Africa, the Public Investment Corporation 25 percent and two Chinese state owned companies, CADF and CITVC, 20 percent (Mail & Guardian). amaBhungane named Interacom Holdings, made up of CADF and CITVC, as the 20 percent shareholder in 2019 (https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2019-11-14-pic-wants-to-investigate-sekunjalo-directors-after-liquidation/), and in July 2026 Daily Maverick still described Interacom as a minority shareholder backed by Chinese investors; no source found reports a sale. Disputed for IOL itself: amaBhungane reported in 2018 that Independent transferred Independent Online to Sagarmatha Technologies, majority owned by Iqbal Survé's family trust, in which Independent held 4.1 percent after a share issue on 31 December 2016 (https://amabhungane.org/iqbal-surves-mythical-beast/); IOL says it has operated as an independent digital publisher, with its own ownership structure, since 2014 (Daily Maverick, 7 June 2026, https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-06-07-iols-r200m-expansion-plan-marks-another-turn-in-the-sekunjalo-media-saga/); Freedom House still described IOL as Independent Media's digital version in 2022 (https://freedomhouse.org/country/south-africa/beijings-global-media-influence/2022). No source found gives Independent's holding in Sagarmatha after 2016 or documents a Chinese state stake in the company that owns IOL now. The record is about ownership; it is not a finding that the shareholders direct what IOL publishes.
foreign_state_stake.source_title: Iqbal Survé threatens to 'expose' M&G, Mail & Guardian, 23 August 2013
foreign_state_stake.state_link: Freedom House calls CITVC a state media company and the China-Africa Development Fund a state policy bank; the Mail & Guardian calls both state owned, and amaBhungane calls CITVC state owned.

foreign_state_stake.held_in: Independent News & Media South Africa (Independent Media), which published Isolezwe until the end of July 2026
foreign_state_stake.holder: Interacom Holdings, the Chinese consortium of China International Television Corporation (CITVC) and the China-Africa Development Fund (CADF)
foreign_state_stake.note: Freedom House (2022) names Isolezwe among the papers Independent Media publishes and reports that a Chinese consortium whose shareholders include CITVC and CADF acquired 20 percent of Independent Media in August 2013; the Mail & Guardian reported the same purchase (https://mg.co.za/article/2013-08-23-00-iqbal-surve-threatens-to-expose-mg) and amaBhungane named Interacom Holdings as the shareholder in 2019 (https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2019-11-14-pic-wants-to-investigate-sekunjalo-directors-after-liquidation/). Sekunjalo said Independent Media's licence to use its mastheads would end on 31 July 2026 (Daily Maverick, 22 July 2026, https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-07-21-sekunjalo-pulls-plug-on-independent-media-amid-murky-r52bn-investment-claim/), and National Media Group, unveiled on 31 July 2026, says it publishes Isolezwe and the other former Independent Media titles under licences from Sagarmatha Technologies (Daily Maverick, 5 August 2026). Ended for Isolezwe, not for Independent Media: Daily Maverick still described Interacom as a minority shareholder of Independent Media in July 2026, and no source found reports a sale. National Media Group's ownership is undisclosed; Sekunjalo says it has a financial stake in it, and no source found documents a Chinese state stake in it. amaBhungane reported in 2018 that Independent held 4.1 percent of Sagarmatha after a share issue on 31 December 2016 (https://amabhungane.org/iqbal-surves-mythical-beast/); no later figure was found. The record is about ownership; it is not a finding that the shareholders directed what Isolezwe published.
foreign_state_stake.source_title: South Africa: Beijing's Global Media Influence 2022 Country Report, Freedom House
foreign_state_stake.state_link: Freedom House calls CITVC a state media company and the China-Africa Development Fund a state policy bank; the Mail & Guardian calls both state owned, and amaBhungane calls CITVC state owned.
